item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.24)] GM's Breakup With CarPlay And Android Auto Has One Exception
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.24)
General Motors is phasing out Apple CarPlay and Android Auto from most of its vehicles, opting instead for native infotainment systems powered by Google's AI assistant, Gemini. However, the 2027 Cadillac Lyriq EV will notably retain support for both CarPlay and Android Auto, a decision attributed to customer feedback. This exception raises questions about GM's broader strategy as it continues to integrate its own AI-driven system while selectively accommodating popular third-party mirroring applications.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.40)] Nvidia's 3-Year-Old H100 Chip Is Still Getting the Market to Pay Up, Jensen Huang Says Compute Is 'Fungible, Durable and Highly Rentable'
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.40)
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reiterated his view that AI computing hardware is a valuable and financeable asset, referring to it as "fungible, durable and highly rentable." This statement comes as the rental price for Nvidia's three-year-old H100 GPUs has climbed 22% in a month to $3.28 per hour, challenging conventional depreciation models for older hardware. Nvidia is also actively working with major financial firms to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure financing, aiming to treat AI chips as a productive, revenue-generating asset rather than depreciating equipment.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (-0.14)] Nvidia supplier Wistron's shares drop after it announces $1.5 billion global stock sale
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (-0.14)
Shares of Nvidia supplier Wistron Corporation fell over 6% after announcing a $1.47 billion global depositary receipt offering. The Taiwanese tech giant aims to raise funds for procuring raw materials and expanding its AI server business, including investments in facilities in Taiwan and the U.S. Wistron, whose shares are up about 23% year-to-date, recently opened its first U.S. manufacturing facility in Texas to produce Nvidia's GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra systems.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.34)] Tech Bytes: Apple prepares US$2,000 foldable iPhone gamble as premium push gathers pace
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.34)
Apple is expected to launch its first foldable iPhone, potentially priced at around US$2,000, alongside the new iPhone 18 Pro range at its September 9 event. This move signifies Apple's deeper push into the premium hardware market and aims to create a new upgrade cycle for consumers. The launch will also highlight Apple's ongoing efforts to advance its AI capabilities with new Apple Intelligence features.

item.title: [MSFT Bearish (-0.27)] Seattle Times and Newsday Sue OpenAI and Microsoft Over AI Copying
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bearish (-0.27)
The Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a federal lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging unauthorized copying of their journalistic content to train and operate AI services like ChatGPT and Copilot. The publishers claim copyright infringement, removal of identifying information, and brand damage, arguing that the AI outputs can replace visits to their websites and reduce revenue. They are seeking damages, injunctions, and the destruction of infringing copies or models.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.23), NVDA Neutral (+0.11)] Jim Cramer Wants Nvidia to Buy Back $500 Billion. Can Apple’s Playbook Work?
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.23), NVDA Neutral (+0.11)
Jim Cramer has proposed that NVIDIA Corporation undertake a $500 billion share buyback, using Apple Inc.'s strategy as a model. While Apple's substantial cash generation supports its buybacks, Nvidia faces different financial demands due to its significant capital commitments for AI infrastructure. The article questions if Nvidia can realistically adopt such a large-scale buyback strategy given its need to preserve flexibility for future growth and market changes.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.31)] Apple's first foldable iPhone is set to debut Wednesday -- and all eyes are on new CEO John Ternus
item.description:

This event marks a significant test for new CEO John Ternus, who recently took over from Tim Cook. The company is under pressure to reignite innovation and address questions about its AI strategy and the aging lineup of existing products.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.21)] Mate Security, Palo Alto Networks, and ServiceNow Join OpenAI’s First-Day Cyber Defense Signatories
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.21)
Mate Security, Palo Alto Networks, and ServiceNow have signed on as first-day signatories to OpenAI's "A Call to Action on Cyber Defense" initiative, which urges cybersecurity vendors, governments, and technology companies to coordinate on AI-powered defense. The initiative highlights the critical need to leverage AI to strengthen cyber defenses against increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled attacks. The participation of these three companies, each with distinct approaches to security, underscores the broad transition towards AI-powered defense as a strategic priority in the cybersecurity market.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.34), NVDA Bullish (+0.24)] Wall Street Is Worried About AMD. Here’s Why Long-Term Investors Shouldn’t Be
item.description:

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.05)] Nvidia Is No Longer Just a Chip Company. It’s the Infrastructure Platform for All of AI
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.05)
Nvidia has evolved from a chip vendor to a full-stack AI factory platform, significantly increasing its revenue per gigawatt with newer generations of technology and securing massive third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Alongside Nvidia, companies like Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, and Intel are also key players in the AI silicon layer, each addressing different aspects of the growing demand for AI compute, interconnect, and foundry services. These five companies are central to the AI buildout, all operating under supply constraints and seeing substantial revenue growth from hyperscaler deployments.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.06)] Microsoft Is Close to a New All-Time High. This Number Will Determine If It Keeps Climbing
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.06)
Microsoft is nearing its all-time high of $549, but its future stock performance hinges on free cash flow amidst surging capital expenditures for AI infrastructure. While robust revenue growth in Azure and AI services presents a bullish case, a significant increase in capex has suppressed free cash flow, keeping the stock rangebound. Investors are advised to monitor Azure growth, quarterly free cash flow, and Copilot seat additions to determine if the stock will break out or remain stalled.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.47), AMZN Neutral (+0.15)] Microsoft Stock Is Building a Trillion-Dollar AI Opportunity. Is $600 Next?
item.description:

Microsoft's stock is positioned for significant growth, with analysts projecting a 22% upside to a $604.89 price target, driven by robust Azure cloud growth, expanding AI monetization through products like Microsoft 365 Copilot, and a massive $678 billion commercial remaining performance obligation. Despite heavy capital expenditure on data centers, the company's strong operating margins and demand exceeding supply signal continued momentum, suggesting a path towards $600 and potentially higher. The article evaluates bull and bear cases, comparing Microsoft's valuation to peers like Alphabet and Amazon, and highlights its unique position in turning AI hype into locked-in revenue.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.20)] BUUU to buy 60% of data-centre builder Brightray, adds $60M in placements

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.46), MSFT Bullish (+0.25)] Why Apple May Be the Safest AI Stock Nobody Calls an AI Stock
item.description:

Despite a high P/E ratio compared to competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet, Apple's superior ROE and operating margins justify its premium valuation. The article provides a bullish price target of $363.99, citing strong earnings, growing services revenue, and the upcoming Siri AI, while acknowledging risks like memory costs and supply constraints.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.32), AMZN Bullish (+0.31)] Powering the AI Boom: Uranium’s $95 Spark
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.32), AMZN Bullish (+0.31)
The article highlights how increasing artificial intelligence electricity demands are driving tech companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta to secure long-term nuclear power agreements. This demand, combined with expiring legacy utility contracts and rising production costs, has led Wall Street analysts to raise long-term uranium price forecasts to about $95 per pound. Key beneficiaries identified include Cameco Corporation (CCJ), NexGen Energy (NXE), and BWX Technologies (BWXT), as they are well-positioned to capitalize on the uranium supply squeeze and the nuclear infrastructure buildout.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.31), AMZN Bullish (+0.32)] Oracle Has Fallen Nearly 20% in 2026: One Wall Street Firm Says It's Going to Double and Then Some
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.31), AMZN Bullish (+0.32)
Oracle's stock has dropped nearly 20% in 2026, even as its cloud competitors have gained, largely due to significant capital spending that resulted in negative free cash flow. Despite this, one Wall Street firm, Guggenheim, maintains a Street-high price target of $400, suggesting the stock could more than double, backed by a massive $638 billion remaining performance obligation (RPO) and a long-term growth outlook in AI infrastructure. Analysts see Oracle as an undervalued opportunity compared to its fully-priced cloud peers, with its next major test being the Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings report on September 10th.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.01)] Nvidia’s Israeli networking business is booming, and so is its economic footprint
item.description:

This expansion has significantly increased Nvidia's economic footprint in Israel, impacting local R&D, employment, and potentially tax contributions, despite the complexities in attributing these figures directly to Israeli exports. The article highlights Israel's growing importance as a hub for AI and data center technologies due to Nvidia's presence.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.11)] Gartner HR Survey Reveals Australian Employees Are Slowly Regaining Confidence in the Job Market
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.11)

This improved confidence is leading to higher job-seeking activity and emerging retention risks for employers, as 26.5% of employees are actively looking for new roles and fewer intend to stay with their current organizations. Poor manager quality and lack of respect are cited as top reasons for leaving, urging employers to focus on career growth, manager quality, flexibility, and meaningful work experiences.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.25), NVDA Bullish (+0.23)] Exclusive: Coursera, Microsoft and Steve Hanke on the Future of Jobs — AI Could Be a ‘Net Job Creator’
item.description:

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.01)] Why Taiwan’s Silicon Shield Is Failing
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.01)
Taiwan's "silicon shield," stemming from its dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, is facing challenges as China invests heavily in chip self-reliance, particularly in mature-node chips. While Taiwan still holds leverage in cutting-edge chips, China's increasing capacity in 28-nanometer chips threatens to make Taiwan's shield irrelevant for its own economy, potentially leading to a more fragile global trade environment with rising chip prices. This shift means that the geopolitical importance of Taiwan's chip production will no longer solely rely on the most advanced technologies, but also on the control of common chip manufacturing.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.03)] Where Does AMD Make Its Processors?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.03)
AMD processors are primarily manufactured in Taiwan by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest semiconductor producer. While TSMC has facilities in Arizona for some AI chips, the final assembly and packaging of AMD CPUs occur in places like Penang, Malaysia, and China. This manufacturing strategy is similar to Nvidia's, with TSMC also producing chips for other major tech companies like Apple and Tesla.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.12)] VinFast Auto (VFS) Quietly Pumps the Brakes on Its India Manufacturing Plans
item.description:

This move comes about a year after VinFast entered the Indian market, which it had targeted for growth following struggles in the U.S. While the company stated it will focus on India-specific models and continues existing assembly, the decision highlights cost pressures and challenges in its global expansion strategy.

item.description:

The Seattle Times and Newsday have filed a copyright infringement lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging their journalism was used without permission to train AI models and that these models reproduce their content. They are seeking the destruction of their works from the companies' data and AI models. This lawsuit mirrors similar actions by other publishers and adds to the growing legal challenges against AI companies regarding intellectual property rights.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.09), AMZN Neutral (-0.11)] Apple (AAPL) Raises Apple TV and Apple One Prices Again in the U.S.
item.description:

item.description:

This move comes amidst ongoing trade tensions and tariff threats, with GM leveraging its financial strength to fortify its North American manufacturing footprint and protect its high-margin pickup and SUV business, although challenges like tariff costs, EV-related expenses, and potential volume declines persist.

item.description:

This move highlights Apple's strategy to bolster its services revenue through commercially appealing films, following the success of its "F1" movie. The article suggests that investing in films like this, even if unconventional, can significantly impact Apple's highly-valued services segment by attracting subscribers to Apple TV.

item.description:
